challenge_facts_addressed.effect_on_judgment: Regular initiation and approximately weekly one-on-one meetings over twelve weeks provide substantial evidence of sustained relational interest, reducing confidence in B.
Helping with an important interview and attending a meaningful birthday dinner demonstrate effort and responsiveness beyond purely passive or incidental involvement.
Independently resuming contact after two periods apart supports continuity of interest and weighs against viewing the involvement as entirely convenience-driven.

reason_for_retaining_or_changing: The challenging facts establish meaningful interest and some investment, but they do not clearly establish commitment. B remains better supported because Casey twice declined to define the relationship without a timeline, generally kept meetings geographically convenient or short-notice, canceled two advance plans for other commitments, did not introduce Drew to close friends or family, and declined planning two months ahead. The evidence therefore points more strongly to sustained but low-commitment involvement than to meaningful commitment, while warranting lower confidence.

revised_recommended_action.explanation: The mixed pattern makes direct clarification appropriate: Casey's consistent contact and supportive actions indicate interest, while the avoidance of definition and longer-term planning leaves the intended level of commitment unresolved.
